summary: Approval link 403 immediately for JIT access requests when user full name contains non-ASCII characters
description:
Issue summary: Users with non-ASCII characters (e.g., accents, umlauts, emoji) in their display/full name receive a 403 when clicking the approval link generated by the Just-in-Time (JIT) access flow. The approval link appears to expire immediately or fail signature validation.

Context: The internal JIT flow issues a one-time approval URL containing a signed token derived from the Okta SAML assertion augmented with user attributes. We observed failures only for accounts where the full name or displayName contains characters outside plain ASCII.

Impact: Affected employees cannot complete temporary elevation for console/admin tasks. This blocks on-call runbook actions and time-sensitive troubleshooting for ~5% of staff (estimated) with non-ASCII characters in their Okta profile.

Environment: internal JIT microservice (approval-service v2.7.1), identity-proxy (v1.8.0), Okta (org: redwoodinc.okta.com). Observed in prod/us-east region and replicated in staging.
impact: Temporary elevation requests fail to be approved; users see 403 on approval link. Blocks on-call and runbook completion for affected engineers. No data leakage observed. Estimated 3–8 users/day hit this during recent rollouts.
environment: prod (us-east), staging (us-east), approval-service v2.7.1, identity-proxy v1.8.0, Okta SAML integration (custom-augment pipeline)
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Ensure Okta user has non-ASCII characters in profile full name (e.g., ‘Joséphine Müller’ or emoji in displayName)
2) Request JIT elevation via internal Support UI (Request -> Temporary Admin)
3) Approver triggers approval and system sends approval URL via Slack/email
4) Click approval link — browser returns 403 immediate with message 'approval token invalid or expired'
5) Inspect approval-service logs for token validation failure and identity-proxy for attribute normalization steps
expected_result: Approval link validates token and applies temporary roles; user receives confirmation and temporary elevation is active.
actual_result: Approval link returns 403 with token validation error. Logs show HMAC/signature mismatch during token verification when original SAML attribute contained non-ASCII characters.
logs_and_links: approval-service stderr snippets: https://logs.redwood.internal/jump/abc123 (redacted) — shows 'token signature mismatch' at 2026-03-10T08:47:12Z
identity-proxy trace: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/xyZ987 — shows attribute normalization UTF-8 -> URL-encoded sequence
Confluence runbook draft: JIT approval flow (internal) — https://confluence.redwood.com/pages/JIT-approval-debug
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:20 - Priya Rao: Reproduced in staging with 'Joséphine Müller' created test account. Approval link 403 consistently.

2026-03-10 10:05 - Liam O'Connor: Noted that approval token is generated by approval-service after receiving SAML attributes via identity-proxy. Token generation uses URL-escaped payload before HMAC signing.

2026-03-10 11:00 - Liam O'Connor: identity-proxy appears to url-encode displayName using encodeURIComponent, while approval-service expects raw UTF-8 bytes when verifying signature — mismatch leads to signature failure.

2026-03-10 14:30 - Eng (auth team) ran end-to-end capture: SAML assertion contained UTF-8 'Joséphine Müller' -> identity-proxy transformed to 'Joséphine%20M%C3%BCller' when forwarding to approval-service header 'X-User-FullName'. Approval-service computed signature over original (non-encoded) value on generation path (legacy behavior), but verification path decodes differently.
2026-03-11 09:00 - Security reviewed: no credential exposure; failure is only in token validation path.

2026-03-11 10:15 - Hypothesis: Mixed canonicalization between services — some components normalize to NFC, some use percent-encoding. Also observed emoji sequences where multi-codepoint grapheme clusters are split on decode path.
workarounds: Manual elevation by SRE: on-call can run adhoc role-assignment script (requires SRE approval) as temporary bypass — documented in runbook (short-term).
Request approver to copy-paste the approval token into the on-call tooling UI (alternate verification) — manual and error-prone.
Create a temporary alias without non-ASCII characters in Okta and request elevation using that account (mitigation, not ideal).
next_steps: 1) Patch approval-service to normalize and percent-encode consistently before signing and verifying (recommended). 2) Update identity-proxy to forward attributes in canonical NFC UTF-8 with clear content-type header, or avoid double-encoding. 3) Add unit/integration tests covering non-ASCII names (accents, emoji, combining marks). 4) Deploy hotfix to staging, run regression, then roll to prod behind a feature flag. 5) Postmortem and add monitoring for token-signature-failure spike metric.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:25 - Priya Rao: Customer (internal user) reported immediate 403 after clicking approval link. Attached screenshot in Slack thread. Asked for priority since on-call runbook blocked.
2026-03-10 10:10 - Liam O'Connor: I can reproduce; starting trace capture for the JIT path. Adding auth team.

2026-03-10 12:02 - Andrés Martinez (Auth): Initial triage — looks like attribute normalization discrepancy between identity-proxy and approval-service. I'll prepare a small patch to enforce NFC and consistent percent-encoding on the proxy side.
2026-03-11 16:40 - Security: Reviewed the flows; no sensitive token leakage. Approve hotfix to staging. Recommend rollback plan and canary release.

resolution: Work in progress: Auth team created identity-proxy PR to stop double-encoding and ensure attributes forwarded as NFC UTF-8. Approval-service patch drafted to perform defensive normalization on verification path. Staging hotfix validation in progress as of 2026-03-12. Follow-up: create monitoring alert for 'approval_token_signature_mismatch.count' and add integration tests for non-ASCII display names.
